author: abdominalbenito
body: Leveling slows to a snails pace at around 100, and grinds to almost an absolute stop approaching 200. Keep that in mind when upgrading and picking items you want to use. author: kryvian
body:
Get a beefy battery pack. You say you'll only be out for an hour at most but you will most likely be returning near midnight if you could, or just 5 hours after you run out of juice.  


It boils down to:   
Mage  
Warrior  
Thief  
With branching out into these, using the above as a "base":  
Bard  
Pet   
Archer  


With team play breaking down into:  
Damage Dealer  
Time mage  
Area of effect magus  
Healer/remove status/revive  


All classes and nearly all combinations are viable, literally pick your flavor and try to follow it.  
Once you reach T7\~T8, go back and look at the classes you didn't buy, see what skills they have that you may find useful; specifically defense and offense buffs, and buy those classes (and the ones you need to get to those classes).  


Specializations are not mandatory, if you don't find anything you like or suits you in the next tier, you don't need to get it. I'm still running a specialization one tier below me because it's more useful to me.  


When you're nearing a class upgrade, make sure your current gear can be used (class mage/warrior/thief/melee) by the class you're moving up to; or have gear that you can use. If you find yourself  that the weapons you saved up for next class are not worth it, you can switch back to the old class charge free. This does not happen for Specializations.  


You can Flee from a dungeon or gauntlet, change gear/pet and come back to the same floor you fled from, with the same remaining health and status effects you had before you fled. Many do this if they find they have the wrong gear.  


You can increase your view distance using the consumable torch, lanterns that you can get off mobs/bosses or from shops, and weapons/side weapons, as well as much later in the game in the form of gems from the third horseman.
